summary.title: OWASP Juice Shop (rebuilt)
summary.description: Rebuilt from Juice Shop's own shipped threat-model.json (old v1.x Threat Dragon format, unreadable by the current app) using its element/flow list as the ground-truth spec. Trust boundaries added from Phase 0 reasoning. 10 confirmed findings attached to the Angular Frontend -> Application Server flow, where every one of them was actually found.

diagrams.title: High Level Data Flow
diagrams.placeholder: OWASP Juice Shop - rebuilt DFD with confirmed findings

threats.title: JWT payload discloses full Users row (password hash incl.)
threats.description: The login response's JWT payload is the entire Users row (id, email, password hash, role, deluxeToken, totpSecret, etc.), not a minimal claims set. Base64URL-decoding requires no key. Token also stored in localStorage, readable by any XSS.
threats.mitigation: Issue a minimal JWT payload (user id + role only); never include password hash or other full-record fields in the token.

threats.title: GET /rest/basket/:id - no ownership check (BOLA)
threats.description: Any authenticated user can read any other user's basket by incrementing the numeric basket id in the URL. Confirmed via curl and Burp: requesting another user's basket id returned their full basket contents.
threats.mitigation: Check basket.UserId against the authenticated user's id before returning basket contents.

threats.title: POST /api/BasketItems - ownership check bypassed via duplicate JSON key
threats.description: The write path's ownership check inspects the first BasketId key in the JSON body; the write itself uses the last. Sending BasketId twice (own basket first, target second) bypasses the check. Root cause: the clarinet streaming parser reports every duplicate key, unlike JSON.parse.
threats.mitigation: Use JSON.parse (or reject duplicate keys) instead of a streaming parser that treats repeated keys as separate values; validate and write using the same resolved value.

threats.title: GET /api/Users - dumps every user to any authenticated customer
threats.description: Registered with only isAuthorized(), no role check. A plain customer token returns the entire user table, including which accounts are admin.
threats.mitigation: Restrict GET /api/Users to an admin role; never return full user records (incl. deluxeToken) to a plain customer token.

threats.title: PUT /api/Products/:id - any customer can rewrite prices
threats.description: The authorization check for this route is commented out in source (changeProductChallenge). A plain customer token can change any product's price.
threats.mitigation: Re-enable the isAuthorized()/role check on PUT /api/Products/:id.

threats.title: No rate limiting on login attempts
threats.description: 8 rapid failed login attempts all returned 401 with no throttling, lockout, or delay. Compounds with the /api/Users user-enumeration finding.
threats.mitigation: Add rate limiting / account lockout after repeated failed login attempts.

threats.title: Issued JWTs carry no exp claim despite expiresIn: '6h' in source
threats.description: authorize() calls jwt.sign(user, privateKey, { expiresIn: '6h' }), but the decoded issued token has no exp claim, only iat - extending a stolen token's useful window indefinitely.
threats.mitigation: Investigate why expiresIn isn't producing an exp claim and fix token issuance so signed tokens actually expire.

threats.title: CORS wildcard (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), no CSP
threats.description: Every response carries an unconditional wildcard CORS header and no Content-Security-Policy. Not currently exploitable via the cookie channel since Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is absent, but still a real least-privilege misconfiguration.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a known origin allowlist instead of a wildcard; add a Content-Security-Policy header.

threats.title: /swagger.yml publicly exposed, unauthenticated
threats.description: The full API schema is served with no authentication, handing an attacker the documented API surface without needing to crawl or guess.
threats.mitigation: Require authentication for /swagger.yml, or exclude the schema from the deployed build.

threats.title: whoami's fields query param has no field allowlist, leaks password hash
threats.description: GET /rest/user/whoami?fields=... applies no allowlist to the comma-separated fields param; any field on the caller's own record (password hash, totpSecret, deluxeToken) can be requested. Identity always resolves from the caller's own cookie, so this is not an IDOR - the bug is the missing field-level allowlist (API3).
threats.mitigation: Apply an explicit field allowlist to the fields= query param in GET /rest/user/whoami, excluding password/totpSecret/deluxeToken.
